If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities, and the Chairman resolves initiative ties. grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then the other firms; ties go to the manager with the most windows, then PM clockwise order. A firm owes £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or firm Value. Pay using either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, it dissolves unless rescued: emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules, pay expenses, discard any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment; alternatively, merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and then cover the endangered firm's shortfall. On dissolution, shares go to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops stay invested. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from the India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on a dividend. Record the total cash actually paid out, not the per-share rate, as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying no dividend records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London after dividends. Firm cash is limited to specified procedures and is not family cash.
